Kharanāda
also khAranAda(dI) a. old med. authority. Q. in a number of med. works an. C.s: in Ātaṅkadarpaṇa,
; by Cakrapāṇi on Caraka, p.. 405, 408 N. S. Press edn. 1965; by Nāganātha in Nidānapradīpa, Mu7nchen

; by Aruṇadatta in Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya; by Hemādri in Āyurvedarasāyana, many times; by Vopadeva an. his father Keśava; by Niścalakara on Cakrapāṇi; by Dakṣiṇāvartanātha an. Pūrṇasarasvatī on Meghadūta.
For the discovery of a leaf from a ms. of the Nyāsa on the Kharanāda a. Gilgit, see Pt. M. S. Kaul, J. Myth. Soc. XXX. i. 1939, p.. 1-12 from which the Kharanāda appears to have been written before 7th Cent. A. D. [Page181-b]
According to Ind. on Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha (Kalpa, ch. 8), the Kharanādasaṁhitā was written by Bhaṭṭāra Haricandra; the Skt. Intro. to Carakasaṁhitā, N. S. Press 3rd edn. 1941, however interprets this a. saying that Haricandra redacted that text. Ind. add. that Kharanādasaṁhitā is mostly a redaction of Caraka (yā ca Kharanādasaṁhitā Bhaṭṭāra-Haricandrakṛtā śrūyate sā ca Caraka-pratibimbarūpaiva lakṣyate p. 338, Trichur edn.).
--C. Nyāsa. fr. discovered among Gilgit mss.
See J. Myth. Soc. XXX. i. 1939; also P. K. Gode, Stud. in Indian Lit. His.. I. p.. 112-31; by Mukhopadhyaya, HIMed. III. p.. 763-70.

Kharapaṭa
eponymous a. of a treatise on theft. Mentioned by Kauṭalya in Artha Śāstra,
/11 an. Mattavilāsaprahasana 11/12; an. in the Tamil epic Śilappatikāram

. ll. 189; also l. 180 an. C.s thereon.
See Tirumalai Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa I (1932) p.. 41-6; see also G. Harihara Sastri, Sir Asutosh Mem. Vol., Calcutta, 1926-8, p.. 224-7, where he argues against the identity of Kh. an. Mūladeva found in a passage (in some readings) in the lex. Hārāvalī q. by Śivarama on Vāsavadatta.
